# `Browser.Storage`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Storage — read from and write to Web Storage (`localStorage`)
over `Ipe.Ffi.Js` ports.

A first-party proof of the per-capability web mechanism spanning BOTH port
directions: outbound `JsCmd`s (`get` / `set` / `remove` / `clear`) request a
storage operation, and an inbound `JsMsg` carries a read's result or an
operation acknowledgement. Both cross the same seal codec and fail-closed port
discipline as every other port; there is no second transport.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses `js-port:storage`
(import-derived, keyed on the canonical `Ipe.Browser.Storage` path prefix via
`WebCapability::for_browser_module`, alias-immune); only the top-level app's
`[capabilities] accepts` set can grant it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.Storage.Internals` publishes the closed outbound/inbound ADTs
    and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` wiring.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `get` returns a
    `Task Error (Maybe String)` via the correlated port→Task bridge (a decoded
    value or `Nothing` for an absent key); `set` / `remove` / `clear` remain
    `Cmd`-shaped, and `changes` is the inbound subscription folding the narrow
    `JsMsg` into a typed `Result Error (Maybe String)`. The inbound `case` is
    EXHAUSTIVE: an unavailability becomes a typed `Err`, never a silently
    dropped variant.

## `get`

```ipe
get : String -> Task Error (Maybe String)
```

`get key` — read the value stored under `key` as a `Task Error (Maybe String)`.

Uses the correlated port→Task bridge (`Js.request`). The served JS handler reads
`localStorage.getItem`; a present key resolves to `Just value`, an absent key to
`Nothing`, and an unavailable store to a typed `Err`.

Importing this module discloses `js-port:storage`; the app must grant it with
`accepts = [ JsPort Storage ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `set`

```ipe
set : String -> String -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`set key value` — write `value` under `key`. Outbound `Cmd`; an unavailable
store traps to a typed inbound result on the `changes` subscription.

## `remove`

```ipe
remove : String -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`remove key` — delete the value stored under `key`. Outbound `Cmd`.

## `clear`

```ipe
clear : Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`clear` — remove every key from the store. Outbound `Cmd`.

## `changes`

```ipe
changes : (Result Error (Maybe String) -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`changes toMsg` — the inbound subscription, wired in `subscriptions`.

The decoder IS the security gate: every inbound value runs through the total,
bounded seal decoder for the narrow `JsMsg`; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is folded EXHAUSTIVELY into a
`Result Error (Maybe String)` — a `Got` carries the read value, a `Stored` /
`Removed` / `Cleared` acknowledgement carries `Nothing`, and an unavailability
becomes a typed `Err`.
